subject: POC qualification: technical criteria & environment charter
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Kim <laura.kim@healthguard.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & POC qualification — next steps and environment options

Hi Laura — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and the proposed lightweight charter so we can scope the POC and get the right environment in place. I captured items from the call and a suggested plan below.

Key objectives (what you want to validate)
- Accuracy and context-handling for patient note summarization (~95% precision on critical fields)
- Token-latency under load for 2 concurrent users (90th percentile < 300ms per token)
- Data isolation & auditability for PHI handling

Candidate environment options (we discussed tradeoffs on the call)
1) Hosted (Redwood API) — fastest start, no infra lift; good for initial model fit and latency baselines.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity) — predictable performance and consistent throughput for multi-user load tests.
3) VPC/private deployment — required if your security team insists on no egress and customer-managed networking (longer lead time).

Suggested minimal success criteria (please confirm):
- Functional: auto-summaries match internal QA set with >= 0.90 F1 on critical fields (Medications, Allergies, Diagnoses).
- Performance: sustained 100 RPS burst with 50 concurrent sessions, 95th percentile request latency < 600ms (end-to-end).
- Security/compliance: audit logs accessible to HealthGuard for the test window; no raw PHI persisted outside your VPC if VPC path taken.

Proposed timeline (target):
- Day 0–3: Technical kickoff + environment choice + NDA/TOU + network questionnaire (if VPC).
- Day 4–10: Environment provisioning + sample data ingest + baseline run on hosted or dedicated sandbox.
- Day 11–21: QA validation, load tests, and model tuning.
- Day 22–25: Demo + decision meeting.

Owners:
- Redwood: Soojin (technical lead), Ben (commercial owner), Marissa (trial ops).
- HealthGuard: Laura (product/ML), SRE/Network contact (TBD).

Attachments: I attached a draft POC success criteria spreadsheet and a short network questions doc; please review and tell me which environment you prefer so we can issue a provisioning checklist.

Next steps (please reply with):
- Preferred environment: Hosted | Dedicated sandbox | VPC
- SRE contact for network work (if VPC)
- Any additional success criteria beyond the above

Thanks,

—

Thanks Soojin — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side:
- We’re leaning toward Dedicated sandbox for this first POC to reduce variability; we want to validate perf at scale before committing to VPC.
- Confirm that audit logs and request traces can be exported to our SIEM (we’ll provide an endpoint).
- Matt (our SRE) will pick up network questions; cc’d him here (matt.sre@healthguard.ai).

On success criteria: we’ll add a data-safety check — redaction/no-storage of raw PHI in logs for non-VPC paths. If Dedicated sandbox can give us a config toggle for log redaction, that’s preferred.

Timeline: tight but workable; aim for your Day 0 kickoff on Friday (28 Jul) if we can get the paperwork out today. Procurement — can you confirm typical paperwork and lead time?

–Laura

Subject: Re: Follow-up & POC qualification — next steps and environment options

Great — Dedicated sandbox sounds like the right initial path. Quick answers and actions from our side:

1) Audit logs / SIEM export: yes, we can push structured event logs to an HTTP(s) endpoint (or S3) for the POC window. We’ll include a config to strip raw text fields unless you explicitly opt in.

2) Paperwork: for a short POC we typically do a simple Letter of Engagement + Data Processing Addendum (DPA). Ben — can you confirm standard turn times and attach a template for HealthGuard Procurement?

3) Network & SRE: Matt, I’ve attached the network questions PDF — if you can share the allowed CIDR ranges, firewall egress rules, and whether you need IP allowlisting for callbacks, that’ll speed provisioning. If dedicated sandbox is preferred we’ll provision reserved capacity in us-west-2.

Detailed POC plan (ops + success criteria) — condensed: 
- Data: HealthGuard provides a representative sample (de-identified if possible) of ~500 notes.
- Model: Redwood will provision a mid-sized open model (quantized) with knob for beam/temperature.
- Validation: HealthGuard QA team will run a 25-case blind review followed by a 500-case automated metric run.
- Acceptance: pass on both QA blind set and >= 0.90 F1 on automated run.

Proposed schedule (confirmed):
- Fri 28 Jul: kickoff (1 hour) + finalize paperwork
- Mon 31 Jul: sandbox ready + sample ingest
- Tue 1 Aug – Fri 11 Aug: tuning and QA runs
- Mon 14 Aug: demo + go/no-go decision

Action owners:
- Redwood: Soojin (tech lead, provisioning), Marissa (trial ops), Ben (commercial / paperwork).
- HealthGuard: Laura (product), Matt (SRE/network), Procurement (PO/paperwork).

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for Fri 28 and attach the Letter of Engagement template.

—
Soojin
